subject: Trident Health — livefeed silence and websocket timeouts (urgent)
messages:
From: Eric Lee <eric.lee@tridenthealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Live demo and production: intermittent silence + WS timeouts

Hi Markus / Grace,

We had a customer-facing demo at 08:45 PT and immediately afterwards started seeing silent gaps in the streaming responses for multiple concurrent sessions. In production we observed increased 502s on the streaming endpoint and occasional WebSocket timeouts (client-side error code 1006). The app shows tokens stop arriving for ~6-12s before the connection resets.

Attached are a trace bundle and a sample of request IDs (request ids included in the file). This is blocking our trial customers — they saw blank stages of the transcript during a live interaction. Can we get an urgent triage? Our ops team is standing by.

Impacted: ~12 sessions during the demo window; p95 latency for streaming up from ~220ms to ~1.8s during the incidents.

Thanks,
Eric

Thanks Eric — and thanks for the artifacts. Markus, looping you and Marissa for immediate engineering triage.

Quick context for the internal team: Trident is in trial and the integration demo going poorly risks pause of the pilot. They reported two parallel failure modes: (1) token stream stalls (clients report silence for ~6–12s) and (2) websocket drop/timeout events after the stall. They captured request ids and some server-side traces, attached above.

Ask: Can engineering (Marissa / Markus) confirm whether this looks like an upstream routing/keepalive regression, or if it's model-side backpressure? Also need an ETA for a mitigation we can offer the customer within the hour.

I have the customer on a dedicated Slack channel and can provide live logs.

—Grace

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: 2028-05-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Live demo and production: intermittent silence + WS timeouts

Thanks — I've pulled the traces. Quick findings:
- We see a tight cluster of 502s correlated with the streaming proxy returning a zero-byte chunk followed by connection close. The proxy logs show an upstream keepalive timeout at the same timestamp.
- p95 token delivery latency spikes line up with a sudden increase in connection-level backpressure: connection write queue grew and the runtime's streaming scheduler stalled for ~7–11s.
- Notably, the normal fallback to smaller-sequence model variants did not trigger because the routing check that evaluates queue length was returning stale metrics for a subset of pods (likely a metrics aggregation race).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (short window):
1) Increase websocket keepalive interval on the proxy to 30s -> reduce false timeouts (config change).
2) Force traffic for Trident's project token to the standby region (failover) for now — this will route them to a separate pool.
3) Temporarily enable a stronger streaming sentinel that injects small no-op bytes to keep the client-side stream alive while we fix the scheduler stall.

I pushed a small tracing flag to capture debug headers for the affected request ids (see attached trimmed trace). If we get confirmation from Ops that the proxy change is safe, we should make the keepalive change immediately.

I'll join the Slack channel and stand by for the change.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engineering Lead, Real-time Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: sample_requests_20280530.json (trimmed) - included inline]
